title: Emergency compatibility shim for tenant upgrades failing on opaque Helm config-merge drift
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: Multiple on-prem customers reported tenant upgrade failures during operator Helm upgrades. Symptoms include controller crashloops, secrets not being picked up by reconciliation, and tenants stuck in 'upgrade-in-progress' for >30m. Root cause analysis shows Helm values produced by older customer charts include opaque YAML anchors and templating results that our operator's post-upgrade manifest merge logic misinterprets, causing a partial CR write and subsequent reconciliation errors. Scope: affects Private/VPC customers using Helm-based operator upgrades with customized tenant overlays (approx 12 customers flagged). Goal: ship a narrow compatibility shim that normalizes legacy opaque values during preflight and performs a surgical livepatch that prevents CR write corruption while allowing a safe helm rollforward.
investigation_notes: 2025-02-20: Customer A reported upgrade failure after operator Helm chart 2.10.0 applied; logs showed 'invalid field type for kvCacheSchema' and controller restarts.
Repro: Created minimal overlay with YAML anchor/merge keys + secret refs; helm template produced subtle scalar-vs-map divergence compared to kube-apiserver canonicalization.

Hypothesis: Our operator's 'merge-apply' stage assumes the manifest from Helm is canonical; older Helm templates produced unnormalized keys (anchors, folded scalars) that our CR projection code then serialized differently causing apply patch mismatch and partial object state.
Telemetry: 12 customer clusters emitted operator reconcile error 0x7d2f with spike on 2025-02-19 03:00 UTC; topologically correlated with upgrades initiated via console.
Edgecase: imagePullPolicy string vs boolean rewrite combined with secretRef placeholder replacement leads to schema conversion path in k8s client that fails strict server-side apply for CRD v1.

Mitigation trial: Local repro applied a compatibility layer that pre-normalized manifest bytes using 'kubectl-sigs/yaml/normalize' before server-side apply; prevented partial writes in 9/10 repro attempts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create cluster with operator 2.9.x and tenant overlay that uses Helm alias/anchors for common labels.
2) Run helm upgrade with 2.10.0 operator chart containing CRD changes (minor schema bumps) and observe controller reconcile loop.
3) Inspect operator logs for 'server-side apply conflict: cannot decode' and check Tenant CR in API for partial fields.
4) Reproduce with helm template that includes folded scalars for secret data and see schema conversion divergence during patch application.
proposed_solution: Deliver a backward-compatible preflight normalization step inside operator's upgrade pathway that: (a) performs a canonicalizeYaml(manifest) pass to remove anchors and normalize scalars; (b) applies a short-lived compatibility shim admission that detects pre-upgrade manifests and rewrites only the problematic fields (imagePullPolicy, secretRef placeholders, anchor-expanded maps) to canonical forms; (c) introduce a targeted hotfix to server-side apply code path to tolerate scalar-vs-map transient diffs during upgrade-only reconciliation. This approach avoids a full chart rewrite and minimizes downstream risk.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix branch): implement normalization util and a small admission shim to run in operator preflight. Add feature-flag 'compat.helm-normalize' defaulted ON for 2.10.1 hotfix.
Phase 2 (validation): run canary upgrades in staging and smoke test with the 12 impacted customer overlays; create an automated matrix test that exercises Helm anchor/alias cases.
Phase 3 (release): cut operator-2.10.1-hotfix, roll out to Dedicated host pools and schedule controlled customer hotpatch windows for Private clusters with guided runbook.
Phase 4 (follow-up): upstream a canonicalization library into our manifest pipeline and deprecate the temporary admission shim in the next minor release after full validation.
acceptance_criteria: All 12 flagged customer repros succeed end-to-end with normalized manifests applied and tenants progress to 'running' state within the normal upgrade window.
Operator health (restart count) returns to baseline within 30 minutes post-upgrade on test clusters.
No regressions in non-upgrade paths; regression tests pass in CI for server-side apply scenarios.
Hotfix rollout instructions and rollback steps are documented and validated with one Dedicated customer.
testing_notes: Unit tests added for canonicalizeYaml to cover anchors, folded scalars, and map-vs-scalar corner cases.
End-to-end matrix: Helm versions 3.2, 3.5, 3.8; k8s versions 1.22, 1.24, 1.26; overlay patterns: anchor-heavy, secretRef placeholders, imagePullPolicy mismatch.
Staging canary: 3 tenants on staging passed; one tenant required a manual secret rebind after normalization — added a follow-up small fix to preserve secret references when placeholder token present.

resolution_summary: Implemented a temporary compatibility shim in operator-2.10.1-hotfix that normalizes Helm output prior to server-side apply and preserves secret placeholders during rewrite. Ran canary on staging and validated fixes for all customer repro patterns. Hotfix release planned with scheduled customer windows; rollback instructions included in runbook. Follow-up work planned to upstream canonicalization into the main manifest pipeline and remove the temporary shim.
postmortem_actions: 1) Add manifest canonicalization to operator's core pipeline (ENG-1000020 planned follow-up).
2) Improve preflight validation to detect non-canonical Helm outputs and warn customers during console-driven upgrades.
3) Add e2e upgrade tests covering Helm anchor/alias cases to CI matrix.
4) Update customer docs with recommended Helm template practices for private deployments.
